title: Chicago after-hours clubs and Dorothy Donegan
summary: Roy recalls Chicago clubs, breakfast dances, and Dorothy Donegan sitting in.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: We used to work at Anise(?) Club, too. I used to go down there and stop there and play with a guy that's a lawyer, a trumpet player. He's on Louis Armstrong's (?). I'm trying to think of his name.

I think so. But he's one of the old-guard cats, you know. I can't think of his name now. I just happened to think of the name of that club, the Anise(?) Club, right off 22nd on Street Club. We'd go to the Anise(?) Club. We'd go to the...was it the Cotton Club? It was a club where they had all faggots dancing. I remember that. [PERHAPS JOE HUGHES' CLUB, WHERE RAY NANCE WORKED IN 1939, AFTER LEAVING HORACE HENDERSON]
Where Jimmie Noone worked [EL RADO CAFE]?
No, Jimmie Noone didn't work there. Tensley(?) had it, a guitar player from Louisville, he had the group there. We used to go down and jam. Then we'd go to Rocket's on 47th Street and jam.
Things were going on back then in Chicago?

Yeah. It would go on late, everything around until about five or six o'clock. Then you had the breakfast dances. It was a ...(?)... That's where I first heard Dorothy Donegan. She sat in with us sometimes. But as a rule... Man, she could play, but she would always lose about
eight bars. Like, if this was thirty-two bars, she'd play eight bars then jump in the release, you know. Because she could play good.
She was very young then, I guess.
Oh yeah. Jesus, that's over forty years ago! She had to be young. If she was old then, she'd be over a hundred!
